points.title: 童年成长
points.description: 大江健三郎出生于日本四国岛爱媛县大濑町的一个医生家庭。童年时期，他深受母亲影响，母亲是位虔诚的基督徒，这为他后来的思想奠定了基础。1945年，日本战败后，大江经历了美军占领时期，这段经历深刻影响了他对战争与和平的思考。他在家乡的森林中度过大量时光，这些自然景观后来成为他作品中的重要意象。1951年，他考入爱媛县立松山高等学校，开始接触文学，并受到法国存在主义哲学的影响。
points.descriptionEn: Kenzaburo Oe was born in Ose, Ehime Prefecture, on Shikoku Island, to a family of physicians. His childhood was deeply influenced by his mother, a devout Christian, which laid the foundation for his later philosophical views. In 1945, following Japan's defeat in World War II, Oe experienced the American occupation period, which profoundly shaped his thinking about war and peace. He spent considerable time in the local forests, which later became significant motifs in his literary works. In 1951, he entered Ehime Prefectural Matsuyama High School, where he began to engage with literature and was influenced by French existentialist philosophy.

points.title: 文学启蒙
points.description: 1954年，大江健三郎考入东京大学法文系，师从法国文学专家渡边一夫。在大学期间，他深入研究了萨特、加缪等存在主义作家的作品，形成了自己独特的文学观。1957年，他在《文学界》杂志上发表短篇小说《奇妙的工作》，获得该杂志的新人奖，正式步入文坛。1958年，他的短篇小说《饲育》获得芥川奖，一举成名。这一时期，他积极参与学生运动，反对《日美安保条约》，这些政治经历成为他早期作品的重要主题。
points.descriptionEn: In 1954, Oe entered the French Literature Department at the University of Tokyo, studying under Professor Kazuo Watanabe, a specialist in French literature. During his university years, he deeply studied the works of existentialist writers such as Sartre and Camus, developing his unique literary perspective. In 1957, he published his short story 'The Work' in the literary magazine Bungakukai, winning the magazine's newcomer award and officially entering the literary world. In 1958, his short story 'The Catch' received the Akutagawa Prize, catapulting him to fame. During this period, he actively participated in student movements against the US-Japan Security Treaty, and these political experiences became important themes in his early works.

points.title: 个人危机与创作转型
points.description: 1963年，大江健三郎的长子大江光出生，患有脑部障碍。这一事件成为他人生的重大转折点，迫使他重新思考生命、责任与文学的意义。他开始关注残障人士问题，并将这一主题融入创作。1964年，他发表《个人的体验》，以自身经历为蓝本，描述了面对残障儿子时的内心挣扎与成长。这一时期，他创作了《万延元年的足球队》等代表作，将个人命运与日本历史、社会问题紧密结合，形成了独特的'大江文学'风格。他还积极参与反越战运动，成为日本知识分子的代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: In 1963, Oe's first son Hikari was born with brain damage. This event became a major turning point in his life, forcing him to reconsider the meaning of life, responsibility, and literature. He began to focus on issues concerning people with disabilities and incorporated these themes into his writing. In 1964, he published 'A Personal Matter,' based on his own experiences, describing his inner struggles and growth when facing his disabled son. During this period, he created representative works such as 'The Silent Cry' (originally published as 'Football in the Year of the Imjin'), weaving personal fate with Japanese history and social issues to form his unique 'Oe literature' style. He also actively participated in anti-Vietnam War movements, becoming a representative figure among Japanese intellectuals.

points.title: 国际声誉与创作巅峰
points.description: 1970年代后，大江健三郎的创作进入成熟期，作品主题更加多元化，包括对日本战后历史的反思、对核武器的批判以及对边缘群体的关注。1986年，他发表《同时代的游戏》，探讨了记忆与历史的关系。1994年，大江健三郎获得诺贝尔文学奖，成为日本第二位获此殊荣的作家，评委会称他'以诗意的力量创造出一个想象的世界，在这个世界中，生活与神话凝聚在一起，为当代困境提供了启示'。获奖后，他更加关注日本的社会问题，特别是宪法第九条和平条款的维护，积极参与和平运动，并继续创作反映时代精神的作品。
points.descriptionEn: After the 1970s, Oe's writing entered a mature period with more diverse themes, including reflections on post-war Japanese history, critiques of nuclear weapons, and attention to marginalized groups. In 1986, he published 'The Game of Contemporaneity,' exploring the relationship between memory and history. In 1994, Oe was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, becoming the second Japanese writer to receive this honor. The Nobel Committee described him as 'who with poetic force creates an imagined world, where life and myth condense to form a disconcerting picture of the human predicament today.' After winning the award, he focused more on Japanese social issues, particularly the protection of Article 9 of the Japanese Constitution (the peace clause), actively participated in peace movements, and continued to create works reflecting the spirit of the times.

points.title: 晚年思想与遗产
points.description: 晚年，大江健三郎更加关注日本的政治走向和社会问题，特别是对日本右翼势力的崛起持批判态度。他发表了《被偷换的孩子》等作品，继续探讨身份认同与历史记忆问题。2006年，他发表《愁容童子》，回顾了自己的创作生涯。尽管健康状况不佳，他仍坚持写作和演讲，积极参与公共事务。2013年，他宣布'封笔'，但仍然关注社会议题。大江健三郎的文学遗产不仅在于其作品的文学价值，更在于他作为知识分子的社会责任感和对和平、人权的坚定立场。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，影响远超日本国界，成为世界文学的重要组成部分。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Oe paid increasing attention to Japan's political direction and social issues, particularly criticizing the rise of right-wing forces in Japan. He published works such as 'The Changeling,' continuing to explore issues of identity and historical memory. In 2006, he published 'A Face Masked with Sadness,' reflecting on his literary career. Despite declining health, he continued to write and speak, actively participating in public affairs. In 2013, he announced his retirement from writing but remained concerned with social issues. Oe's literary legacy lies not only in the literary value of his works but also in his sense of social responsibility as an intellectual and his firm stance on peace and human rights. His works have been translated into many languages, influencing beyond Japan's borders and becoming an important part of world literature.

supporter.zh: 大江健三郎被誉为日本战后文学的旗手，他的作品深刻反映了日本社会的创伤与转型。支持者认为，他通过文学直面战争、核武器、残障人士等敏感议题，展现了知识分子的勇气与良知。他的诺贝尔文学奖不仅是对个人成就的肯定，更是对日本文学与世界文学对话的贡献。大江健三郎将个人命运与国家历史紧密结合，创造了独特的文学风格，为日本文学注入了新的活力，同时也为世界文学提供了理解日本战后社会的重要窗口。
supporter.en: Oe is hailed as a leading figure in post-war Japanese literature, whose works deeply reflect the trauma and transformation of Japanese society. Supporters believe that through his literature, he confronted sensitive issues such as war, nuclear weapons, and disabilities with the courage and conscience of an intellectual. His Nobel Prize was not only recognition of his personal achievements but also a contribution to the dialogue between Japanese and world literature. By weaving personal destiny with national history, Oe created a unique literary style that injected new vitality into Japanese literature while providing an important window for the world to understand post-war Japanese society.

critic.zh: 批评者认为大江健三郎的作品过于西化，忽视了日本传统文化中的美学价值。一些评论家指责他的政治立场过于激进，特别是对日本战后历史的批判被视为'自虐'。此外，他的作品晦涩难懂，语言风格复杂，影响了大众读者的接受度。还有人批评他将个人家庭问题过度文学化，利用儿子的残障作为创作素材，有消费亲人之嫌。在政治立场上，他被批评为'反日'，对日本传统价值观的否定也引发了争议。
critic.en: Critics argue that Oe's works are overly Westernized, neglecting the aesthetic values of traditional Japanese culture. Some commentators accuse him of having overly radical political positions, particularly his criticism of post-war Japanese history being viewed as 'self-flagellation.' Additionally, his works are often considered obscure and stylistically complex, affecting their accessibility to general readers. Others criticize him for overly literaryizing his personal family issues, using his son's disability as material for creation, which they see as exploiting his family. Politically, he has been criticized as 'anti-Japanese,' and his negation of traditional Japanese values has also sparked controversy.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，大江健三郎被视为日本战后知识分子的代表人物，他的创作轨迹反映了日本从战败到经济腾飞再到泡沫破裂的历史进程。他的作品不仅是文学成就，更是重要的历史文献，记录了日本社会的集体记忆与创伤。大江健三郎的'边缘人'视角——关注残障者、原住民、少数族裔等群体——使他成为日本社会批判的重要声音。在流行文化中，他被视为'良心知识分子'的象征，代表了日本知识界对和平、民主与人权的坚持，同时也被视为连接日本文学与世界文学的重要桥梁。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Oe is regarded as a representative figure of post-war Japanese intellectuals. His creative trajectory reflects Japan's historical journey from defeat to economic boom and then to the bubble burst. His works are not only literary achievements but also important historical documents that record the collective memory and trauma of Japanese society. Oe's perspective on 'marginalized people'—focusing on individuals with disabilities, indigenous peoples, and ethnic minorities—has made him an important voice in Japanese social criticism. In popular culture, he is seen as a symbol of the 'conscientious intellectual,' representing the Japanese intellectual community's commitment to peace, democracy, and human rights, while also being recognized as an important bridge connecting Japanese literature with world literature.

self.zh: 文学不是逃避现实的手段，而是面对现实、改变现实的武器。
self.en: Literature is not a means of escaping reality, but a weapon for facing and changing reality.

others.zh: 大江健三郎是日本战后文学的良心，他以非凡的勇气和深刻的洞察力，揭示了日本社会的创伤与矛盾，为人类提供了面对困境的智慧。
others.en: Kenzaburo Oe is the conscience of post-war Japanese literature. With extraordinary courage and profound insight, he has revealed the traumas and contradictions of Japanese society, providing wisdom for humanity to face its predicaments.
